description: redacted_refusal_text falls back to the read-only or RLS text for an unrecognised refusal message, giving the model the wrong kind of refusal.
config-loading.md list of sub-sections setting extra='forbid' omits RuleSetsConfig.
mysql_connect_kwargs docstring does not mention the ValueError raised for a URL with no user/host or a non-numeric port.
RuleSetsConfig can hold file set with loaded None; consumers read that as no rule sets (fails open), though no shipped path reaches it.
Lists inside frozen records are mutable, LoadedRuleSets is a mutable dataclass, CatalogConfirmation.confirmed can be set without its lock.
RuleSetRefusal.kind is a free str placed into client text; TableRule.row_rule is typed Any.
_url_database strips one leading '/' while build_sql_runner uses lstrip('/'), so a '//' path compares a different database name.
No test drives a rule-set refusal through the MCP query_database tool in server.py.
Preflight branch for a failed information_schema read (non-RuleSetCatalogError) is untested.
ensure_catalog_confirmed logs only type(exc).__name__ for a non-RuleSetCatalogError failure; detail only in the traceback.

factory.md:65 (and factory.py:186-188 comment) says build_agent forces allow_memory_writes off under a rule-set file; track_usage=allow_memory_writes is set at factory.py:152 before the gate at line 189, so retrieval still writes usage counters.
changelog.d/389.added.md:8-9 'saves nothing to memory' overstates: usage counters and timestamps are still written on retrieval.
verify-memory comment in cli.py says the rule-set check runs before every other argument and config check; config loading runs first.
rule-sets.md:3 verified-against marker names 537f0a4; the code it describes changed in c0ac928.

safety/__init__.py, whole_row.py:197 and read-only-safety.md:17,207 still say the whole-row guard sits directly beneath result masking; RefusalRedactingRunner now sits between them under a rule-set file
RuleSetSelection checks none of its invariants when built; only select_rule_set enforces them
RuleSetFile.rule_sets accepts an empty list, so a file with no sets loads and every request is refused

src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:35, src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py:197 and docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:17 and :207 still say the whole-row guard sits directly beneath result masking; with a rule-set file configured RefusalRedactingRunner sits between them, and read-only-safety.md's new Composition with rule sets section contradicts line 207.

The comment above _PARSE_REFUSAL_MARKERS in src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py says test_safety_rule_sets pins every marker, but test_every_read_only_parse_refusal_redacts_as_a_parse_refusal reaches neither 'could not resolve SQL dialect' nor 'empty parse tree'.

TableRule in src/sqllens/rule_sets.py compares column names case-sensitively for duplicate columns, duplicate predicate columns and columns/predicate_columns overlap, though MySQL column names ignore case; the catalog check later rejects such files but with a letter-case error instead of naming the duplicate.
